name: Peru
system_note: Congress has unusually strong power to remove presidents.
snapshot: Keiko Fujimori won the presidency on her fourth attempt in 2026, after a decade in which Congress removed or forced out president after president.
culture: Peru was the heart of the Inca empire, and Quechua and Aymara are still widely spoken. Machu Picchu and Cusco draw visitors from around the world. Lima is a world food capital, with ceviche and a Japanese-Peruvian fusion called Nikkei. Mario Vargas Llosa, who died in 2025, won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
society: Peru has had seven presidents since 2016, several of them jailed. Mining of copper, gold and silver drives the economy, and the central bank has kept inflation low despite the chaos. Informal work dominates. Deadly protests after the ouster of Pedro Castillo in 2022 exposed deep divides between Lima and the southern Andes.
situation: Peru has had nine presidents in ten years. They have been impeached, jailed, forced out by Congress or have resigned in disgrace, and in 2022-23 protests against the political class left about 50 demonstrators dead. In 2026, Peruvians gave the job to the most familiar name in their politics.

Keiko Fujimori, daughter of Alberto Fujimori, the 1990s president who defeated the Shining Path insurgency and then turned authoritarian before being jailed for human rights crimes, finally won on her fourth try. After a first round in which she took just 17 percent among 35 candidates, she beat leftist congressman Roberto Sánchez in the 7 June runoff with 50.135 percent, a margin of 49,641 votes out of 18 million (MercoPress). Sánchez initially refused to recognise the result. Fujimori campaigned on crime, especially the extortion gangs that have terrorised bus drivers and small shopkeepers, promising four new prisons plus one modelled on El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison, with inmates forced to work (AP via Las Vegas Sun). She took office in July. Whether she lasts a full term, in a country where Congress routinely removes presidents, is the real question.
power: A presidential republic with unusually strong congressional checks: the unicameral Congress can remove a president for "moral incapacity," a vague clause it has used repeatedly. The president is directly elected for five years with a runoff and cannot serve consecutive terms. A new Senate returns in 2026.
holders: President Keiko Fujimori (Fuerza Popular), in office since July 2026.
